sentences: Deterministic decomposable negation normal form is a circuit representation supporting useful counting and reasoning operations.
Decomposability separates variables at conjunctions, while determinism separates satisfying cases at disjunctions.
The question asks whether negating such a representation can always be done efficiently within the same class.
A small representation of a set need not directly describe its complement.
The project studies whether this compilation language is robust under a basic logical operation or can suffer a substantial representational blowup.

context_blocks.text: The power and resource requirements of computational models. A lower bound must cover every algorithm or circuit in the specified class.

The separate polynomial-size existence question is TCS-7260. A polynomial-time complementation algorithm as asked for here implies a polynomial size bound, but the converse is not established. The two targets are retained separately so that an existence result is not mistaken for an efficient construction.

context_blocks.text: The knowledge-compilation map asks for polynomial-time negation of deterministic DNNF and its smooth variant. This is constructive closure, including polynomial output size, and is stronger than nonconstructive polynomial-size closure; the latter remains separately represented by TCS-7260.
